tool_args.old_string: \looseness=-1 We presented the first systematic comparison of three execution-free verification formulations (\cls{}, \cwm{}, \traj{}). At function level, \cls{} and \cwm{} are statistically equivalent (TOST $p{=}0.007$, 5 seeds); \traj{} reaches parity on Qwen3 but not DeepSeek-Coder (2.69\pp{}). Per-test classification achieves 217$\times$ throughput while providing diagnostic signal whose downstream benefit was not confirmed ($n{=}44$, $p{=}0.42$). Complementary errors (oracle: 90.63\%/95.83\%) motivate complexity-aware routing. At repository level under ${\leq}$8B LoRA fine-tuning, a robust interaction ($z{=}-23.7$) confirms divergence (19--26\pp{}, single-seed variant-level), with \cwm{} falling below majority baseline---consistent across families but dependent on multiple confounds (\S\ref{sec:threats}). \cls{} is recommended for throughput; behavior at larger scale remains open~\cite{meta2025cwm}.
tool_args.new_string: We presented the first systematic comparison of three execution-free verification formulations (\cls{}, \cwm{}, \traj{}). At function level, \cls{} and \cwm{} are statistically equivalent (TOST $p{=}0.007$, 5 seeds); \traj{} reaches parity on Qwen3 but not DeepSeek-Coder (2.69\pp{}). Per-test classification achieves 217$\times$ throughput while providing diagnostic signal (benefit unconfirmed; $n{=}44$, $p{=}0.42$). Complementary errors (oracle: 90.63\%/95.83\%) motivate complexity-aware routing. At repository level under ${\leq}$8B LoRA fine-tuning, a robust interaction ($z{=}-23.7$) confirms divergence (19--26\pp{}, single-seed variant-level), with \cwm{} falling below majority baseline---consistent across families but dependent on multiple confounds (\S\ref{sec:threats}). \cls{} is recommended for throughput; behavior at larger scale remains open~\cite{meta2025cwm}.
